name: Missing Authorization
principle: The product lets an actor access a resource or perform an action without checking whether that actor is authorized. This exposes privileged data or functionality to users who are only authenticated, anonymous, or authorized for a different object.
detection_signals: Spring @RequestMapping/@GetMapping/@PostMapping handler lacks @PreAuthorize/@PostAuthorize/@Secured and contains no SecurityContext/hasAuthority/isUserInRole check
Servlet doGet/doPost uses request.getParameter("id") to read/update/delete data without request.isUserInRole(...) or ownerId == request.getUserPrincipal() check
public REST/RPC method performs delete/update/export/admin/config action before any role/permission/ACL check
DAO/repository call findById/save/deleteById uses user-controlled id without filtering by currentUserId/tenantId/ownerId
C/C++ request handler dispatches privileged command based on user input without caller uid/role/capability check
file/database/resource open/read/write on user-supplied identifier occurs before access-control function such as checkAccess/canRead/canWrite/acl_allow
route or command registered in dispatcher table without requiredRole/permission metadata while adjacent privileged routes have it
negative_signals: @PreAuthorize/@PostAuthorize/@Secured or equivalent annotation enforces the needed permission on the handler
server-side check compares resource.ownerId/tenantId to current authenticated user before access
central filter/interceptor/middleware maps the exact route/action to required role and denies by default
query constrains access with current user or tenant, e.g. findByIdAndOwnerId(id,currentUserId)
explicit ACL/RBAC call such as accessController.checkPermission(user,action,resource) gates the operation
operation is intentionally public/read-only and accesses only non-sensitive public resources
false_defense_traps: Authentication check only, e.g. user != null, with no authorization for the action or object
Hiding the button/link in the UI while the server endpoint remains callable directly
Client-side JavaScript role checks without matching server-side enforcement
Prepared statements or input validation without an authorization decision
Role check only, e.g. ROLE_USER, without object ownership or tenant check for peer users
verification_focus: Does every sensitive resource/action have a server-side authorization decision for the current actor before the operation executes?

consequence_chains.trigger: A protected page or endpoint is directly requested without a server-side authorization gate
consequence_chains.consequence: Unauthorized forced browsing to privileged functionality or data

consequence_chains.trigger: Read path lacks authorization for sensitive application data
User-controlled object id is used without checking ownership or tenant
consequence_chains.consequence: Horizontal authorization bypass across users with the same role

patch_principle: Enforce default-deny authorization at every server-side boundary for sensitive pages, APIs, commands, and resources.
Map roles, permissions, actions, and resources explicitly; use RBAC/ACL checks tied to business logic.
Check object-level ownership or tenant membership, not only coarse roles.
Use vetted authorization frameworks or centralized filters/interceptors, but verify route coverage.
Perform the authorization check before reading, modifying, deleting, or returning the protected resource.
